takeaway: Sticky Pacific-moisture weekend: Costa Rica’s service flags the ITCZ still active, with possible early showers on western Nicoya and isolated afternoon rains across Pacífico Norte; Nicoya heat stays sharp (around 34°C). Surf winds remain Pacific/onshore — Papagayo light/variable Saturday after a brief morning easterly, with southwest–west elsewhere, then south to southwest into early next week; early checks only, not glassy all-day offshore. Distant East Pacific storms (Hurricane Rachel near Baja, Hurricane Nolo west of Hawaii) stay well away; a new low south of southern Mexico still has a high (~80%) chance of forming within a week and should drift west-northwest. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sat–Mon)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service says the Pacific moisture band (ITCZ) stays unstable this weekend — possible early rains on the western Nicoya Peninsula and near the gulf, then mostly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers across Pacífico Norte; nights stay mostly cloudy with scattered rains. Nicoya heat remains sharp (around 34°C). Weekly guidance: humid Pacific inflow into the weekend with early coastal rains possible and afternoon storms more widespread inland; no tropical waves crossing the next few days. Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate (typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine) Saturday into Monday, with U.S./European means and the AI ensemble broadly agreeing on a moist but not extreme Pacific-side day. Official longer outlook still keeps northern Pacific on the drier-than-normal side this week (roughly 5–90 mm Pacífico Norte for 28 Sep–4 Oct). Near-surface Papagayo: Saturday morning easterly–southeasterly about 10 kt becoming light/variable under 5 kt, with southwest–west about 10–15 kt elsewhere; overnight trending south; Sunday–Monday south to southwest about 10–15 kt.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before isolated afternoon storms; expect sticky air and possible early western-Nicoya showers. For surf, treat Saturday–Monday as Pacific/onshore–side days: light/variable Papagayo after a brief morning easterly is not glassy all-day offshore. Early checks only.
periods.confidence: High that Saturday–Sunday stay ITCZ / Pacific-moisture days with scattered storms and no nearby cyclone threat. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how firmly weekend southwest–west onshore holds at the beach hour to hour.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Tue–Fri)
periods.pattern: Official weekly guidance expects continued humid Pacific inflow without another tropical wave in the near term, and Pacífico Norte remaining quieter than peak rainy-season weeks. Ensemble averages show continued moist Pacific-side days into midweek — often light to moderate daily totals near Nicoya — without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Longer official outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal into early October (next week roughly 1–70 mm for 5–11 Oct). Marine winds hold south to southwest through Tuesday. A new East Pacific low could form south of southern Mexico late weekend / early next week and drift west-northwest away from Costa Rica. Mid-level maps stay mixed midweek — trust the marine surface call for beach wind while it still favors Pacific/south flow.
periods.implications: Keep midweek plans flexible for quick storms. Surf-wind quality looks weaker than trade-offshore days: expect Pacific/south–southwest flow and choppier faces early in this window, with only early checks for any leftover glass. Nicaragua is not showing a clean all-day offshore signal for Nosara mornings through at least early next week.
periods.confidence: Moderate for a quieter-than-peak Pacífico Norte theme; low–moderate on exact wet-day timing and how firmly early-week onshore winds hold past Tuesday.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from early into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged for the current week. Ensemble means still allow some moist days into mid-October, and the U.S. tropics outlook (updated 29 Sep, valid 7–20 Oct) notes model support for a possible broader Central American rain-gyre pattern early in its week-2 window (around Oct 7 onward) — worth watching, not a locked-in flood spell. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west; formation odds south of southern Mexico stay high (~80%) through seven days.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes; re-check midweek if a gyre signal firms up.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail and for any week-2 gyre risk past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No focused gyre window over Costa Rica now; weekly outlook sees no tropical waves in the next few days. Broader week-2 (around Oct 7+) gyre mention in U.S. tropics guidance remains a longer-range watch only.
gyreWatch.supporting: Active Pacific moisture band is bringing humid, showery conditions into the weekend. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby offshore. Some ensemble means keep light-to-moderate Pacific-side rain into early next week. U.S. tropics outlook notes model support for a possible Central American gyre early in week-2. Distant East Pacific storms keep the far-Pacific moisture field active near Mexico, and a new low may form south of southern Mexico mid–late next week.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Saturday Pacífico Norte forecast is isolated showers under Pacific-moisture factors, not a multi-day washout. Weekly outlook: no tropical waves the next few days. Longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October, with no extreme event flagged for this week. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico / Hawaii, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Pacific / onshore (Papagayo light/variable Sat after brief E–SE morning → S–SW Sun–Tue)
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters (marine forecast issued Sat 1:17 a.m. PDT): Saturday morning easterly to southeasterly about 10 kt becoming light/variable under 5 kt; elsewhere southwest to west about 10–15 kt with scattered showers. Overnight light/variable Papagayo becoming south about 10 kt late, with southwest–west elsewhere. Sunday–Tuesday: south to southwest about 10–15 kt. Mid-level maps are mixed midweek — trust the marine surface call for beach wind while it still favors Pacific/south flow. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as glassy all-day offshore. Nicaragua is not offering a clear all-day offshore quality signal for Nosara this stretch.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early checks only Saturday–Tuesday. Expect choppier Pacific/onshore–side flow most of the day. No clean all-day offshore / Caribbean-trade signal this period.
surfWinds.confidence: High on the marine forecast trend (light/variable Papagayo Saturday, then south to southwest Sunday–Tuesday). Moderate on exact hour-to-hour beach winds Saturday while Papagayo stays light/variable, and on any midweek wind shift past Tuesday.
